svg.title: Four kinds of sandbox
svg.desc: A restricted process, a container, a stand-in for the operating system, and a small virtual machine. Each walls the command off in its own way, and each fails in its own way.
svg.text: Restricted process
Same computer, same operating
system core as you. A rule on the
command hides the rest of it.
Codex and Claude Code put the shell here.
Starts quickly. The policy lists which
files and which network addresses
the command may use.
Failure: the policy blocks a call a tool
needs, or the helper program is absent
and the command runs as your user.
Container
Its own files and process list.
It shares the host's operating
system core. Docker is a common one.
The image is the starting filesystem:
the repo, the compiler, the packages.
Failure: the memory limit or the disk
limit is hit, the runtime stops, or the
image lacks the program the model called.
A container nested inside another
often lacks a fresh process list.
Stand-in system
A program answers the command's
requests itself. The real operating
system receives that narrow set.
Stronger separation than a normal
container, with a cost in speed and
in compatibility.
Failure: a build tool asks for a call
the stand-in handles differently,
and the test behaves unlike your laptop.
The room is up, and the command is wrong.
Small virtual machine
It has its own operating system.
Cursor gives each cloud agent
a machine of this kind.
Boot is a real machine start, shortened
with snapshots of a prepared disk.
Failure: the machine runs out of memory
or disk, the host reaps it while idle,
or restoring the snapshot fails.
The harness on the other computer
still holds the transcript.
